meta.title: 3I/ATLAS comparative heliospheric reconstruction
meta.sourcePolicy: Quantitative comparisons are extracted from unchanged archived runs. Claude’s finer-cadence animation is regenerated separately with unchanged numerical kernels and retained boundary inputs, using an output-only host hook; its verification is recorded in the animation provenance.
meta.referenceOverlayRevision: 2026-10-18: higher-precision native ENLIL export; helium conversion applied once. Agent reconstructions and metrics unchanged.

comet.clock: Photon-arrival UTC at the geometric Earth proxy
comet.bandQualification: Claude: transferred 12-member assimilation-design 16th–84th percentiles. Probability coverage has not been calibrated.
notes: Linear resampling at 30-minute intervals; null outside native coverage. Exact native samples, not display resampling, are used for metrics.
Argon and Claude geometric UTC are mapped to arrival UTC using copied Horizons Earth–comet separation. Codex retains its recorded arrival UTC.
Native published PN means differ in clock and integration convention; use the homogenized exact-GTI table for direct comparison.
ENLIL is an independent remote-driven model, not an observation of the comet. Density is converted from rho/mp to proton density assuming 5% alpha particles.

argon.scaleMeaning: PN exposure-weighted mean count rate / PN exposure-weighted model incident flux

nativeMeanComparison.explanation: Native report averages 10-minute rows selected by a GTI mask. Exact endpoint integration gives 2.16876e8 on the geometric clock (+3.06%); the ~15.7-minute photon delay gives 2.21305e8 on the common arrival clock (+2.04% further).

codex.scaleMeaning: PN exposure-weighted mean count rate / PN exposure-weighted model incident flux

nativeMeanComparison.explanation: Native final report already uses exact PN GTI integration and the observer-arrival clock. The common value reproduces the native selected CT report.

claude.scaleMeaning: PN exposure-weighted mean count rate / PN exposure-weighted model incident flux

nativeMeanComparison.explanation: Native report uses a fine midpoint GTI quadrature on geometric UTC. Exact geometric integration reproduces 1.45478e8; the ~15.7-minute photon delay changes the sampled SIR spike to 1.40065e8 on arrival UTC (−3.72%).

xray.qualification: The curves are flux-driven X-ray shape proxies, each scaled to the observed exposure-weighted mean. None of the models predicts absolute counts: heavy-ion charge states, abundance, neutral coma and instrumental response remain unconstrained. The eight observed rates were not used to tune the wind. Pearson r measures shape agreement; it is not empirical plasma accuracy or a statistical model probability.
xray.integration: Exact trapezoidal integration of each native piecewise-linear curve over every accepted PN GTI, with exact endpoints and no extrapolation. Common photon-arrival UTC for all agents.
xray.rateUnitEvidence: Manuscript Supplement, solar-wind/lightcurve discussion: net rate spans 0.55–4.29 counts s−1. The 10⁻³ surface-brightness contour unit elsewhere is a different quantity.
xray.source: Copied preprint EPIC-pn 0.2–1 keV background/oot-corrected lightcurve and accepted GTIs; ObsID 0963720201.

spacecraft.label: STEREO-A / PLASTIC
spacecraft.qualification: The models are compared with spacecraft measurements on the same finite hourly samples, 19 Nov–5 Dec 2025. Argon and Claude assimilated these spacecraft; Codex also used spacecraft data in calibration. These residuals therefore include calibration performance. Ratios give model / observation.

coronalReplication.title: Independent PFSS/SCS/WSA versus archived CCMC WSA 5.4/GONGz
coronalReplication.qualification: Claude’s independently computed PFSS/SCS/WSA boundary is compared pixel by pixel with archived WSA maps derived from remote sensing. This tests coronal-model agreement. Argon and Codex use the archived maps as input and have no separate coronal replication.

boundaryMap.title: Remote-derived WSA boundary before heliospheric propagation
boundaryMap.qualification: GONG photospheric magnetograms constrain PFSS/SCS topology. WSA converts open-field expansion and coronal-hole distance into an empirical speed map near 0.1 AU. All three reconstruction families use this modeled boundary input.

evidence.limit: Coronal mapping and closure uncertainties propagate to comet timing and density.
Different boundary pressure/density conventions; low spacecraft skill in this interval.
Final Argon and Codex references omit explicit CMEs; Claude includes selected cones. Composition is not predicted.
No contemporaneous heavy-ion composition constraint at the comet; cannot validate absolute SWCX counts.

charts.title: Brio–Wu shock tube: retained native density profiles

series.label: Codex native Athena CT N=8192 (PPM/RK3 benchmark)

charts.notes: Standard gamma=2, t=0.1 setup. Claude retained a plot and error table but no numerical 1D profile; its refinement errors are shown separately. Codex uses the production CT kernel with higher-order PPM/RK3 reconstruction and time integration; production uses PLM/RK2. Brio–Wu admits multiple compound-wave branches, so the plotted references are identified by method and resolution.

charts.title: Shock-tube density error under refinement
charts.notes: The test definitions and self-reference resolutions differ between models. Compare refinement trends within each series. Shock discontinuities reduce global convergence order toward one. The Codex series includes only the selected CT formulation.

charts.title: Spherical steady wind: error against analytic radial solution
charts.notes: Each analytic reference uses its benchmark’s archived boundary and pressure convention. The two setups differ. Codex verifies its final CT implementation through separate flux/geometry audits and the recorded numerical controls below.

charts.title: Claude linear MHD waves: double-precision verification
charts.notes: Amplitude 10⁻⁶. Float64 twin establishes nominal second-order accuracy; production float32 reaches a small-amplitude rounding floor.

metrics.qualification: Two published plateau samples; PPM/RK3 benchmark, not production PLM/RK2; no retrospective pass threshold
GLM divergence drift remains; not converged to roundoff

benchmarks.notes: Each panel identifies its benchmark, reference solution, precision, pressure convention and aggregation rule. These differences limit comparisons of error magnitude across models.

animation.sampling: Uniform x/y nodes including endpoints; flat frame index = yIndex * width + xIndex, y increases upward.
animation.projection: Sun-centered J2000 ecliptic x/y, viewed from ecliptic north; vernal equinox to the right.
animation.timeConvention: Physical geometric UTC; common exact 6-hour cadence, bounded linear temporal interpolation between native slices.

argon.nativePlane: Constant solar latitude −6.455° (conical shell), projected to J2000 ecliptic x/y
argon.qualification: Retained movie slices are available for the 160-cell baseline run. The quantitative comet comparison uses the 224-cell fine run. The animation samples the solar-latitude cone at −6.455° and projects it onto the display axes; an ecliptic slice would require additional output.

claude.qualification: The retained density and radial-speed slices give radial proton flux n_p v_r. The full velocity vector required for n_p |v| was not retained.

codex.qualification: Native double-precision CT conserved-state interpolation. Missing outside retained cell-center support, including r≳2.293 AU. No density/speed auxiliary slices were retained.

animation.contrastDefinition: Native proton flux multiplied by the squared heliocentric radius in its source sampling surface, in AU². This compensates for radial geometric dilution to show stream structure.
animation.qualification: Colors, spatial display limits, frame timestamps and tracks are shared. Native planes and flux definitions differ and are labeled. Projection cannot supply a missing physical slice; values are not cross-model difference maps. Null/zero-code pixels are unavailable, not zero wind. No simulation has been rerun.

homogenization.units: Proton number density cm⁻³; speed km s⁻¹; proton flux cm⁻² s⁻¹; all time axes MJD UTC.
homogenization.missingData: JSON null; animation encoding 0. Never extrapolated or replaced with synthetic plasma.
homogenization.quality: Spacecraft metrics use the same positive finite observed/model timestamps for all three final references. In-sample calibration is explicitly separated from benchmark verification and independent forecast accuracy.
homogenization.xray: Common exact PN GTIs, photon-arrival UTC, exposure-weighted mean normalization. Counts are illustrative flux-driven shape proxies, not absolute SWCX predictions.
homogenization.nativeMeans: Native report values may differ because clocks, GTI quadrature, resolutions and alpha corrections differ. The common exact-GTI table is recomputed from retained native outputs.
knownInconsistencies: Argon prose holdout metrics disagree with machine-readable summary_results.json; this application prioritizes native numeric files.
Argon movie uses base160 while comet reference uses fine224; final Codex movie has no separate speed or density channels.
Claude movie is radial n v_r, while Argon/Codex movies use n |v|. Native plane projection differences cannot be removed without new 3D output.
